title: Nanosecond Nanothermometry with Time-Resolved EELS in a STEM
content: Understanding thermal transport in nanostructures is crucial for fundamental and technological reasons, especially as devices shrink towards the nanometer scale. Studying out-of-equilibrium behavior in these structures requires access to fast timescales, typically from picoseconds to microseconds. Existing methods that provide both high temporal and spatial resolution remain limited [1]. However, recent advances in event-based direct detectors for electron microscopy [2] open exciting new possibilities.
